subject: Private fleet patch escrow & network bridge plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@hightower.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private fleet patch escrow & network bridge plan

Hi Sam —

Following our call last week, I put together a short plan for the upcoming private-fleet maintenance that covers two things you asked about: (1) escrowed patch delivery and version pinning, and (2) a temporary L2/L3 bridge approach to keep cross-subnet control plane traffic stable during kernel and NIC driver updates. Attached: patch_escrow_matrix_v2.xlsx and bridge_vlan_diff.patch.

High level proposal:
- Maintenance window: Dec 14, 02:00–06:00 PT (targeting minimal user impact; can shrink to 02:00–04:00 for the canary wave).
- Version pinning: ship patches to an escrow bucket and stage onto canary nodes; default pins for production nodes updated via PR with an automated 24h hold before rollout.
- Canary plan: 3 canary hosts (one per AZ) -> 20% of cluster -> observe 12h for perf/telemetry before bulk.
- Network bridge: temporary routed bridge on the management VLANs to avoid ARP churn when NIC drivers reload; automated ACLs to lock down cross-subnet traffic during cutover.
- Rollback: image rollback + KV store replay cutoff + forced client-side TTL for 10 minutes to flush bad states; we keep a second pin set (last-known-good) for immediate re-pin.

Open asks for you:
1) Confirm the maintenance window availability for your SRE on Dec 14.
2) Ok to create a read-only egress ACL that we then relax post-canary?

I linked a draft runbook in the Drive folder and created a placeholder JIRA (INF-2486) for runbook tasks. If that works, we’ll lock the pin TTL and schedule the canary.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Technical Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: patch_escrow_matrix_v2.xlsx (Excel - matrix), bridge_vlan_diff.patch (diff)

From: Sam Green <sam.green@hightower.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch escrow & network bridge plan

Logan —

Thanks for the concise plan and the attachments. A few constraints from our side:
- We can support Dec 14 but only if the initial canary is restricted to non-production traffic (analytics ingest only).
- Our security team requires a roll-forward checklist in addition to rollback: if a kernel change causes OOMs, we need an explicit short-circuit to throttle request rates and surface a degraded mode.
- For the bridge approach, we prefer an implementation that avoids broad ARP proxying — would the VLAN patch be scoped to the management subnet only?

Also: our procurement/legal asked whether patch escrow delivery can be notarized (checksum and time-stamped delivery) — GlacierCloud Support will also be on standby for driver binaries if we need vendor-signed blobs.

Can you add the short-circuit throttle step to the runbook and confirm the VLAN scope?

—Sam
Sam Green
SRE Lead, Hightower Analytics

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch escrow & network bridge plan

Sam —

Appreciate the constraints; all reasonable. Quick answers and updates:

- Canary scope: we’ll lock canary to analytics ingest hosts only (non-prod slice). I’ll add an explicit label in the deployment manifest so orchestration only targets that label.
- Roll-forward short-circuit: added a throttle step that sets admission controller rate to X=0.5 (configurable) and flips a traffic-shed flag in the load balancer. I added the step in maintenance_runbook_draft.md (Drive link).
- VLAN scope: bridge will be management VLAN only — we’ll avoid ARP proxying on tenant subnets. The attached bridge_vlan_diff.patch contains the exact iptables/nftables rules; GlacierCloud Support is CC'd for driver/binary delivery and checksum stamping.

Operational plan summary (new items):
1) Pre-flight (T-72h): snapshot of control-plane VMs, export KV snapshot with TTL-preserve off.
2) T-24h: stage escrow patches to S3 with SHA256 and timestamped manifest; legal will receive notarized manifest.
3) Canary wave (Dec 14 02:00–04:00 PT): deploy to A/B canaries; LVL checks (latency, error-rate, driver logs).
4) Observability hold (T+12h): confirm no regressions; if good, schedule bulk wave next maintenance bucket.
5) Emergency rollback: immediate pin to last-known-good using automated re-pin job, then orchestrated node-drain and image rollback. If KV mismatch appears, we run the stored replay cutoff and set client TTL to 10m.

I opened INF-2486 and attached the draft runbook; link is in the related_links list. If you and your security team agree, we’ll add the notarized manifest step to the T-24h checklist and request GlacierCloud to sign the driver blobs by EOD Thursday.

Logan

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet patch escrow & network bridge plan

All —

I’m signed off on the plan with two operational caveats:
1) Canary rollback latency: if we hit a regression, we will initiate immediate re-pin and set the LB traffic-shed for 5 minutes to allow KV reconciliation; ops to verify that re-pin completes within 2 minutes in our staging perf tests.
2) Network verification: prior to driver reload, run the bridge verification script (bridge_vlan_diff.patch includes the test harness section) and confirm no L2 loops. If any loop detected, abort and fail closed to last-known-good.

Karthik — please open INF-2486 tasks for the short-circuit throttle implementation and the notarized manifest handoff. Marissa — once those are in place, book Dec 14 02:00–06:00 PT and mark the first two hours as canary-only.

I’ll join the on-call bridge for the canary wave.

Irene Choi
Head of Production Security, Redwood Inference
